originality.rationale: Nearest published unary partial-Steiner extension formula counts matchings in leaves but not multi-new-vertex coupling. Lugo gives two-involution local statistics; Puder–Zimhoni supplies broader general pattern asymptotics for the probabilistic step, not the concrete finite partial-Steiner extension partition function. The result explicitly credits all underlying matching and Poisson machinery and claims only the coupled weighted all-fixed-arity law. Historical unindexed enumeration is residual risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent r-colour involution-motif enumeration or finite partial-design embedding probability may be in unindexed older work.
Puder–Zimhoni Theorem 2.6 may imply the local fixed-pattern moment step; only the explicit finite diagram reduction and weighted packing law are assessed as new.
A specialist may regard the evaluated fixed-arity partition function as an immediate corollary of a more general unpublished or differently titled enumeration.

value.rationale: Provides a canonical all-fixed-arity finite relational extension spectrum, reducing a constrained 3-uniform incidence problem to the labelled partial-Steiner packing polynomial. Its limiting law specifies the distribution over all internal triple systems, independent fair external pair-presence choices on uncovered pairs, and a nine-way equal-frequency phenomenon at three new vertices; these are motivated objects rather than arbitrary slices.
